accuracy.evidence: Checked against Common Core 4.NF.B.3c ('Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction'), the Common Core progression for Number and Operations—Fractions 3–5, and the DfE National Curriculum in England Year 5 fractions statements. Every sum recomputed: 2 3/5 + 1 4/5 = 3 7/5 = 4 2/5; 5 3/4 − 3 1/4 = 2 2/4; 4 2/6 = 3 8/6 so 4 2/6 − 1 5/6 = 2 3/6; 13/5 + 9/5 = 22/5 = 4 2/5; 1 2/5 + 2 3/5 = 4; challenge items 1 3/5 + 2 4/5 = 4 2/5, 4 1/4 − 2 3/4 = 1 2/4, 3 9/8 = 4 1/8, 3 2/3 = 11/3, 6 5/8 − 4 2/8 = 2 3/8, 3 4/5 + 2 4/5 = 6 3/5. Parameterised answers (a+b, 5w+2, w−1, a+b+1) were checked at the corners of their ranges by gate_items, and each keeps the fraction part fixed so the whole-number answer is exact.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the errors documented in the fractions research (Common Core progression notes; NCETM Year 5 fractions guidance; Lortie-Forgues, Tian and Siegler 2015 on fraction arithmetic errors): adding denominators (step 1 predict '3 7/10', m1, tag addbot), leaving an improper fraction (3 7/5, m3, tags unfin and whole), losing the regrouped whole (3 2/5, tags lost and drop), subtracting smaller from larger whatever the order (step 3 predict '3 3/6', p4, tag flip), negative fraction parts (tag neg), changing the denominator when subtracting (m2, tag botsub), and converting 2 3/5 as 2 + 3 or 2 × 3 fifths (step 4 choices, m4, tags plus and times).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). 480 Mixed numbers and improper fractions only converts; 902 adds fractions with different denominators; 521 adds simple fractions below 1. This lab is about operating on mixed numbers: dragging one mixed number onto another and swapping 5 fifths for a whole, taking wholes and parts away piece by piece, breaking a whole into sixths when the parts run out, cutting wholes into fifths to count an improper fraction, and jumping wholes then parts on a number line.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each move: after joining, the row shows 3 wholes and 7 fifths with 5 of them outlined, and the swap gives 4 2/5; taking a fourth whole or a second quarter is refused with the reason; in the regroup task the third sixth cannot be taken until a whole is broken, and the 'left' readout shows 3 8/6 becoming 2 3/6; cutting wholes into fifths makes the count reach 13; jumping 2 wholes from 1 2/5 lands on 3 2/5 and three fifth-jumps land on 4.

predictions.evidence: Step 1 asks 2 3/5 + 1 4/5 with '3 7/10' (adding denominators) and '3 2/5' (losing the whole) tempting; the bars give 4 2/5. Step 3 asks 4 2/6 − 1 5/6 with '3 3/6' (5 − 2 taken the wrong way round) tempting; breaking a whole gives 2 3/6.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Every distractor in the eight challenge questions has its own tag and WHY message in mixd_art.js: addbot, lost, flip, neg, drop, whole, plus, times, botsub, unfin, addinstead and wholesonly. In the lab, the improper-fraction choices have their own message for each wrong number (5, 6, 5, 4, 2 2/5, 4 1/5), and over-taking, taking parts that are not there, breaking a whole needlessly and overshooting on the number line each give a specific message.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py gives the kid text grade 1.8 (limit 6.5) and the adult text 7.9 (limit 9.5). Kid sentences are short ('Fifths plus fifths are still fifths.'), and the precise terms for the band (mixed number, improper fraction, numerator, denominator, like denominators, regroup) are in the key idea and adult text, with 'regrouping' explained in the kid text where it is used.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases. The four kid paragraphs match the add, regroup, take-away and improper-fraction steps; the adult text gives the standards, what each task does with its numbers, and the named mistakes; every hint points to a step the learner can take (swap 5 fifths, break a whole, multiply then add).

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (Android, 2x) for every step at start, mid Show me and end, in light and dark themes, plus desktop (gate_browser on iPhone 13 and 1200 px). Bar widths are computed from the canvas width so 4 wholes and 8 parts fit at 360 px. After the first pass the improper-fraction step showed 'undefined' once finished and its running list ran off the edge; the finished state now shows each conversion on its own line, and the canvas was made taller so the 22-fifths grid and the list both fit above the feedback box.

accessibility.evidence: gate_browser passed: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, all 5 tasks complete with Show me, no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (Put them together, Swap 5 fifths for 1 whole, Take away a whole, Take away a quarter or sixth, Break a whole into sixths, Cut a whole into fifths, answer buttons, Jump 1 whole, Jump 1 fifth), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with what is left, the regrouped amount, the fifths counted and the number-line position.
